_comment: Hand-curated core-government entities: root, Crown, Federal Executive Council/Cabinet, 16 Commonwealth Departments (per the AAO of 13 May 2025, amended 1 July 2025), High Court, and Federal Court. Minister-holder data lives in parliament.generated.json (generated from live APH CSVs) and is cross-referenced here by entity id. Department Secretaries: only the 4 independently confirmed via PM&C's published secretary-appointments list are populated; the rest are left without a current OfficeholderTerm (honest 'vacant/unconfirmed' rather than guessed) pending the AGOR ingest adapter (Phase 2).

entities.name: The Australian Electors
entities.description: All Australian citizens aged 18 and over enrolled to vote under the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918. Voting is compulsory. Electors directly elect members of the House of Representatives and senators, who together make up the Parliament that, under the Constitution, holds ultimate legislative authority.

entities.name: The King
entities.description: His Majesty King Charles III is Australia's Head of State under section 61 of the Constitution and the Australia Act 1986, which ended all residual constitutional links to the UK Parliament while retaining the shared Crown. The King acts on the advice of Australian ministers and is represented in Australia by the Governor-General.

entities.name: Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia
entities.description: The King's representative in Australia, appointed under section 2 of the Constitution on the advice of the Prime Minister, formally for an indefinite term (by convention around five years). Exercises the Crown's executive power (s61) on the advice of the Federal Executive Council, and holds reserve powers exercisable at the Governor-General's own discretion in rare constitutional circumstances.

dataSource.name: Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia

entities.name: Federal Executive Council
entities.description: The constitutional body (ss62-63) that formally advises the Governor-General in exercising executive power. Membership comprises all current ministers (and some former ministers), sworn as Executive Councillors. In practice it gives formal legal effect to decisions already made in Cabinet.

entities.name: Cabinet
entities.description: The peak decision-making body of the executive government. Unlike the Federal Executive Council, Cabinet has no basis in the Constitution or statute - it operates entirely by convention. It comprises senior ('Cabinet') ministers chaired by the Prime Minister; decisions are then formally ratified by the Federal Executive Council.

entities.name: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth policy and legislation for agriculture, fisheries, forestry, biosecurity, and food standards.

entities.name: Attorney-General's Department
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth law and justice policy, including constitutional law, the legal system, national security law, and corporate/competition law frameworks.

entities.name: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
entities.portfolio: Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth climate, energy, environment protection and water resource policy and legislation.

entities.name: Department of Defence
entities.description: Administers the Australian Defence Force and Commonwealth defence policy, procurement, and national security capability.

entities.name: Department of Education
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth schools, higher education, and early childhood education policy and funding.

entities.name: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth employment services, workplace relations law, and skills/vocational training policy.

entities.name: Department of Finance
entities.description: Administers the Commonwealth Budget's expenditure side, public sector governance, government property, and government business enterprises.

entities.name: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
entities.description: Administers Australia's foreign policy, diplomatic missions, consular services, trade policy, and overseas development assistance.

entities.name: Department of Health, Disability and Ageing
entities.description: Administers Medicare, the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme, aged care, and (jointly with the NDIA) disability support policy.

entities.name: Department of Home Affairs
entities.description: Administers immigration, citizenship, border protection, cyber security and national emergency management policy.

entities.name: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth industry policy, science and research funding, and resources/energy-production portfolios.

entities.name: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
entities.portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
entities.description: Administers national infrastructure and transport policy, regional development programs, telecommunications/media regulation, sport and the arts.

entities.name: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
entities.description: Supports the Prime Minister and Cabinet, coordinates policy across the whole of government, and administers Indigenous affairs programs and the honours system.

entities.name: Department of Social Services
entities.description: Administers social security policy, families and communities programs, and housing/homelessness policy.

entities.name: Department of the Treasury
entities.description: Administers Commonwealth Budget revenue policy, macroeconomic and fiscal policy, and financial system regulation frameworks.

entities.name: Department of Veterans' Affairs
entities.description: Administers compensation, rehabilitation and support services for current and former Australian Defence Force members and their families.

entities.name: High Court of Australia
entities.description: Australia's highest court, established under s71 of the Constitution. Interprets the Constitution, hears appeals from state and federal courts, and exercises original jurisdiction in matters such as disputes between the Commonwealth and the states. Comprises a Chief Justice and six other Justices, all appointed by the Governor-General in Council.

entities.name: Federal Court of Australia
entities.description: A superior court created by the Federal Court of Australia Act 1976, hearing most civil disputes arising under Commonwealth law (including corporations, competition, intellectual property, native title, migration, and admiralty matters) and appeals from the Federal Circuit and Family Court. Has around 50 judges nationally; only the Chief Justice is modelled in this first version (full bench deferred to a later phase).
